mainTopic: Doing Temple service from outside the עזרה, whether partly entering the עזרה counts as entering, and היתר versus דחייה for impurity
overview: The גמרא asks why סמיכה, which the פסוק also describes as 'לפני ה׳', can be done from outside the עזרה. The answer is that a person can reach his hands in. The גמרא pushes back that שחיטה could also be done from outside with a long knife. It answers that this view follows שמעון התימני, who requires the slaughterer himself to be inside, and it brings a ברייתא to prove it. Then עולא quotes ריש לקיש: a טמא who puts his hand into the עזרה gets מלקות, because partly entering counts as entering. רב הושעיא challenges this from a ברייתא about a טבול יום מצורע on ערב פסח who is allowed to put his thumb and toe into the עזרה. Along the way, רבי יוחנן comments that keeping a טבול יום out of the מחנה לויה is only a rabbinic rule. עולא answers that the מצורע is a special case: since the Torah allowed his partial entry despite his צרעת, it is allowed despite his קרי too. רב יוסף applies this idea to a community that is mostly impure on פסח, and the amud ends with a debate over whether a היתר or a דחייה is the broader idea.

steps.title: Placing hands is also described as 'before the Lord'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: סמיכה is also described with the words 'לפני ה׳', so why should it be treated differently from שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for סמיכה too the תורה writes 'before the Lord'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that 'לפני ה׳' rules out someone who cannot stand in the עזרה. The same words appear for סמיכה, which is not treated that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view under discussion uses 'לפני ה׳' to say a certain service must be done by someone standing inside. If that is how the words work, they should limit סמיכה in the same way, since the פסוק uses them there too. The גמרא wants to know why the two services are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning or pressing one's hands on the head of a קרבן
Before the Lord, meaning inside the area of the עזרה
It is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: Regarding placing hands, it is also written:
"Before the Lord"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading of 'לפני ה׳' by pointing to סמיכה
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לפני ה׳' excludes a person who cannot stand inside the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear for סמיכה, so the same limit should apply there too

steps.title: He can reach his hands in to place them
steps.stepSummary: With סמיכה, a person standing outside can put his hands into the עזרה and lean on the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible for him to put his hands inside and lean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סמיכה can still be done 'before the Lord' by someone outside. He just reaches his hands in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the hands need to be inside the עזרה for סמיכה, so the person's body can stay outside. That is why 'לפני ה׳' does not stop him from doing סמיכה.

phrases.english: It is possible that he brings his hands in and places them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: the service can be done from outside
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סמיכה should be limited by 'לפני ה׳' just like שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: For סמיכה the hands can be put inside, so the limit does not apply

steps.title: Slaughter could also be done with a long knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: שחיטה could also be done from outside by using a long knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: With שחיטה too, it is possible to make a long knife and slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer back on itself. If reaching in works for סמיכה, it should work for שחיטה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person outside the עזרה could use a long knife to slaughter an animal standing inside. So the difference between סמיכה and שחיטה seems to disappear.

phrases.english: Slaughter too is possible,
where he makes a long knife and slaughters!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחִיטָה נָמֵי אֶפְשָׁר דְּעָבֵיד סַכִּין אֲרוּכָּה וְשָׁחֵיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 2 by applying the same logic to שחיטה
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between סמיכה and שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A long knife lets someone slaughter from outside, just as reaching in lets him do סמיכה from outside

steps.title: This follows שמעון התימני
steps.stepSummary: The view being discussed follows שמעון התימני, who requires the slaughterer himself to be inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is שמעון התימני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming whose opinion this is. For שמעון התימני, a long knife does not help because the slaughterer must be inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that a long knife could physically work. It says this view follows a תנא who holds the slaughterer's own hands must be inside the עזרה. The proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Shimon HaTimni.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the long-knife challenge by assigning the view to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A long knife would let someone slaughter from outside
steps.terutzMaskana: According to שמעון התימני, the slaughterer himself must be inside, so a long knife does not help

steps.title: The ברייתא showing שמעון התימני's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an argument. The תנא קמא says only the animal must be 'before the Lord'. שמעון התימני says the slaughterer must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And he shall slaughter the bull before the Lord.' This means the bull must be before the Lord, but not the slaughterer. שמעון התימני says: How do we know the slaughterer's hands must be further inside than the animal? The פסוק says 'And he shall slaughter the bull before the Lord', meaning the slaughterer of the bull must be before the Lord.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that שמעון התימני really holds this view. It also shows that the first opinion disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions read the same פסוק. The תנא קמא connects 'לפני ה׳' to the animal, so the slaughterer may stand outside. שמעון התימני connects it to the slaughterer, so even a long knife would not help.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says only the animal must be 'before the Lord'. שמעון התימני says the slaughterer must be too, so for him a long knife does not help.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"And he shall slaughter the bull before the Lord"
but the slaughterer need not be before the Lord.
Shimon HaTimni says:
From where do we know that the hands of the slaughterer must be
further inside than the slaughtered animal?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר לִפְנֵי ה׳״ –
phrases.english: The verse says: "And he shall slaughter the bull before the Lord"

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹחֵט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר יְהֵא לִפְנֵי ה׳.
phrases.english: the slaughterer of the bull must be before the Lord.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4's attribution to שמעון התימני with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That שמעון התימני requires the slaughterer to be inside the עזרה

steps.title: A טמא who puts his hand inside gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes ריש לקיש: a טמא who puts his hand into the עזרה gets lashes, because entering partly counts as entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of ריש לקיש: a טמא who put his hand inside gets lashes. The פסוק says 'She shall not touch any holy thing, and she shall not come into the מקדש.' It compares coming in to touching. Touching with part of the body counts as touching, so coming in with part of the body counts as coming in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about putting only a hand into the עזרה. It connects to the earlier idea of reaching hands in from outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש learns this from a פסוק that puts touching a holy item next to entering the מקדש. Touching even with a finger counts as touching. So entering even with a hand counts as entering, and a טמא who does so gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, links two things in one פסוק (a היקש)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that partly entering the עזרה counts as entering. That will matter for anyone who reaches a hand inside.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Reish Lakish said:
An impure person who put his hand inside is lashed.
As it says: "Any holy thing she shall not touch, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4. The 'etc.' points to the next words: 'and into the מקדש she shall not come.'

phrases.english: It compares entering to touching:
just as touching with part of the body counts as touching,
so too entering with part of the body counts as entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: whether putting a hand inside counts as entering
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא who puts his hand into the עזרה gets מלקות, because partial entry is entry

steps.title: רב הושעיא begins a challenge from a מצורע on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא starts to challenge עולא from a ברייתא about a מצורע whose eighth day falls on ערב פסח, who became טמא from קרי and immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא challenged עולא: a מצורע whose eighth day fell on ערב פסח, and he saw קרי that same day, and he immersed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the rule of עולא and ריש לקיש. This step only lays out the case. The ברייתא's ruling comes in step 8, and the actual challenge comes in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has a person who is still טמא for that day but needs to finish his purification so he can eat the קרבן פסח. The setup is building toward the question of whether he may put part of his body into the עזרה. That would test whether partly entering really counts as entering.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who is becoming טהור
The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is brought
A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא
And he immersed in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished here. This step only describes the case. The actual question against עולא comes in step 10, after the ברייתא's ruling and a side comment from רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya raised an objection to Ulla:
A leper whose eighth day fell
on Passover eve,
and he had a seminal emission that day, and he immersed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the rule in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that partly entering the עזרה counts as full entry
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: a case of a טמא who needs to finish his purification at the עזרה. The ruling follows in step 8, and the attack itself is stated in step 10 (וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּיאָה בְּמִקְצָת שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה).

steps.title: The Sages let this טבול יום enter because of קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: unlike other טבול יום people, this מצורע may enter, because a מצוה with כרת (פסח) overrides a מצוה without כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said: even though any other טבול יום may not enter, this one may. It is better that a positive מצוה that carries כרת should come and push aside a positive מצוה that carries no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב הושעיא is using against עולא. This sets up the challenge that comes in a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a טבול יום (someone who immersed today but must wait for nightfall) may not enter. Here the חכמים make an exception, because bringing the קרבן פסח carries כרת and outweighs the entry rule, which carries no כרת. This 'weighing' reasoning is what רב הושעיא will use in his challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today but is not fully pure until nightfall
Spiritual cutting-off, a very severe punishment

phrases.english: The Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין טְבוּל יוֹם אַחֵר נִכְנָס,
phrases.english: Even though another טבול יום does not enter,
this one does enter;
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מצורע from the ברייתא, whose eighth day fell on ערב פסח.

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב יָבוֹא עֲשֵׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: it is better that a positive mitzva that has כרת should come
and push aside a positive mitzva that has no כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין טְבוּל יוֹם אַחֵר נִכְנָס, זֶה נִכְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב הושעיא began quoting in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a מצוה with כרת overrides a מצוה without כרת, applied to the טבול יום מצורע on ערב פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the מצורע whose eighth day fell on ערב פסח.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: by Torah law there is no restriction at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the ban on a טבול יום entering the מחנה לויה is only rabbinic, proven from the 'new courtyard' in the days of יהושפט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: by Torah law there isn't even a positive מצוה here. As it says, 'And יהושפט stood in the congregation of יהודה and ירושלים, in the House of ה׳, before the new courtyard.' What is 'the new courtyard'? רבי יוחנן said: it is where they made new rules and said that a טבול יום may not enter the מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side comment from רבי יוחנן on the ברייתא. He says the rule keeping a טבול יום out was not from the Torah at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated the restriction as a Torah-level עשה (without כרת). רבי יוחנן says it is even weaker: the Torah does not forbid it at all. The 'new' courtyard got its name because the Sages made a new rule there, keeping a טבול יום out of the מחנה לויה.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule
The Levite camp, the area of הר הבית

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is talking about the מחנה לויה (the Temple Mount area), not the inner עזרה. Entering the עזרה itself is a different, more serious matter.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה – אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה אֵין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: By Torah law, it does not even have a positive מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means: no Torah מצוה at all keeps a טבול יום out of this area.

phrases.english: As it says:
"And יהושפט stood in the congregation of יהודה and ירושלים,
in the House of ה׳, before the new courtyard" —
What is "the new courtyard"?
רבי יוחנן said:
That they made new rules there (many),
phrases.notes: The word 'many' is in round brackets: the standard printed גמרא has it, but some versions leave it out.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ: טְבוּל יוֹם אַל יִכָּנֵס לְמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה.
phrases.english: and they said: a טבול יום may not enter the Levite camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה – אֲפִילּוּ עֲשֵׂה אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment disagreeing with the ברייתא's assumption that a Torah עשה is involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law a טבול יום may enter the מחנה לויה; the ban is a rabbinic rule made at the 'new courtyard'.

steps.title: How can the מצורע put his hand into the עזרה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא finishes his challenge: if partial entry counts as entry, the טבול יום מצורע could not put his thumb into the עזרה, since both sides carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that partial entry counts as entry, how does he put his hand in for the thumbs? Both this and that are positive מצוות that carry כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא now delivers the actual attack on עולא. He uses the ברייתא to show that putting in a hand should not count as entering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע must put his thumb and toe into the עזרה to receive blood and oil. If that counts as entering, it is a טבול יום entering the עזרה, which carries כרת just like skipping the קרבן פסח. With both sides equal, the 'better to override' reasoning fails, so the ברייתא's permission must mean partial entry is not entry.

keyTerms.meaning: Partial entry, putting in only part of the body
This one and that one, both

phrases.english: And if you say
partial entry is called entry,
how does he put his hand in for the thumbs?
phrases.notes: The מצורע sticks his hand and foot into the עזרה so blood and oil can be put on his right thumb and big toe.

phrases.aramaic: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי עֲשֵׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כָּרֵת הוּא!
phrases.english: This and that are each a positive mitzva that has כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּיאָה בְּמִקְצָת שְׁמָהּ בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי יוחנן's side comment to complete the challenge begun in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's statement in the name of ריש לקיש that partial entry counts as entry (step 6).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If partial entry counts, the מצורע's hand-entry would be a כרת-level violation equal to the פסח, so it could not be overridden. Since the ברייתא permits it, partial entry must not count.

steps.title: עולא: a מצורע is a special case
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the מצורע is different: since the Torah allowed his partial entry for his צרעת, it is also allowed despite his קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: from your own load! A מצורע is different. Since he was permitted for his צרעת, he was permitted for his קרי too.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב הושעיא and keeps his rule that partial entry counts as entry. He says the מצורע is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah itself lets an impure מצורע put his thumb and toe into the עזרה for his purification. Once that impurity was set aside for this act, his extra impurity from קרי is set aside as well. In fact, the need for a special permission shows that partial entry normally does count, so רב הושעיא's own case supports עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: From your own load, meaning your own case proves my point

steps.whatToRemember: עולא stands firm: partial entry counts as entry. The מצורע is an exception, because once the Torah allowed his hand-entry despite his צרעת, it is allowed despite his קרי too.

phrases.english: He said to him: from your own load —
phrases.notes: עולא is speaking to רב הושעיא. Literally 'from your burden': your own question helps my side.

phrases.english: a מצורע is different,
since he was permitted despite his צרעת,
he was permitted despite his קרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הושעיא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the source is a special exception and does not disprove the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's permission for the מצורע to put in his hand shows that partial entry is not entry.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partial entry is entry; the מצורע is permitted only because the Torah's permission for his צרעת also covers his קרי.

steps.title: רב יוסף applies עולא's logic to a mostly-impure community
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that according to עולא, if most of the people were זבים and then became טמאי מתים, they may bring the פסח despite their זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: עולא holds that if most of the people were זבים and then also became impure from a corpse, since they are allowed to bring the פסח despite the corpse-impurity, they are also allowed despite their זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף takes עולא's 'since he was permitted for one impurity, he is permitted for the other' idea and applies it to a new case about the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the community is טמא מת, they may bring the פסח in impurity, but זבים normally may not. רב יוסף says עולא would let the corpse-permission 'carry over' to cover the זיבה too, just as the צרעת permission covered the קרי.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a certain bodily discharge that makes them impure; they normally may not bring the פסח.
People made impure by contact with a dead body.
Most of them, meaning the majority of the community.
The impurity status of a זב.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Ulla holds:
if most of them were zavim
and then they became impure from a corpse,
since they were permitted regarding their impurity,
phrases.notes: When most of the community is impure from a corpse, the פסח may be brought in impurity.

phrases.english: they are permitted regarding their ziva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends עולא's answer in step 11 to a new case involving the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא, a majority who are זבים and then become טמאי מתים may bring the פסח despite their זיבה.

steps.title: אביי says the cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: in this case the corpse-impurity was permitted, but the זיבה, which came first, was never permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these alike? The corpse-impurity was permitted, but the זיבה was not permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's comparison and says the order of events ruins it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the מצורע, his first status (צרעת) already came with permission, and the קרי was added afterward. Here the first status, זיבה, was forbidden from the start. A permission that arrives later for the corpse-impurity cannot erase a ban that was already in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? A way of rejecting a comparison.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Is it comparable?!
The impurity was permitted,
phrases.notes: He means the corpse-impurity, which came second.

phrases.english: the ziva was not permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's comparison of the זבים case to the מצורע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the מצורע case the permitted status came first. In the זבים case the forbidden status came first, so nothing can carry over to cover it.

steps.title: אביי suggests the reverse order
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether רב יוסף meant the reverse: first טמאי מתים, and then they became זבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps this is what the Master means: most were impure from a corpse and then became זבים; since they were permitted regarding their corpse-impurity, they are permitted regarding their זיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a corrected reading of רב יוסף's statement that would match the מצורע case better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the permitted status (corpse-impurity in a majority) comes first, and the זיבה is added later. This matches the מצורע pattern, where צרעת came first and קרי came after.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying.
The Master, a respectful way of addressing a scholar.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Perhaps this is what the Master is saying:
most of them were impure from a corpse
and they then became zavim;
since they were permitted regarding their impurity,
are they permitted regarding their ziva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repairs the problem raised in step 13 by flipping the order of the impurities.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רב יוסף mean the case where the corpse-impurity came first and the זיבה second?

steps.title: רב יוסף agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף confirms that this reversed order is what he meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף agrees to אביי's corrected reading of his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His statement now refers to a community that was first טמאי מתים and later became זבים. That fits the 'permitted first, extra impurity later' pattern of the מצורע.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the case is טמאי מתים who later became זבים.

steps.title: Full permission versus only being pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: Even in the reversed order the cases differ. The מצורע has a full היתר, while impurity in a community is only דחויה, so it may be pushed aside for corpse-impurity but not for זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still not comparable. For a מצורע it is a full permission, so once it was permitted, it stays permitted. But impurity is only pushed aside: it was pushed aside for this kind of impurity, and not for that kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison again, this time with a deeper reason that holds even after the order was fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah fully permits the מצורע's partial entry, so that permission covers any other impurity he picks up. Bringing the פסח in impurity is not a true permission; the ban is only set aside, and only for the specific impurity involved (טומאת מת). So it does not stretch to cover זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Only pushed aside, not truly permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: This step argues that a full permission (היתר) carries over to an added impurity, while a rule that is only pushed aside (דחויה) reaches no further than the specific impurity it was pushed aside for. רבא argues the exact opposite in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Fixing the order in step 14 did not save רב יוסף's comparison. The difference here is about what kind of permission it is, not about which impurity came first.
steps.whyThisMatters: The distinction between טומאה הותרה and טומאה דחויה comes up again and again in the laws of impurity in a community.

phrases.english: But still, it is not comparable;
a leper, it is a full permission,
since it was permitted, it was permitted.
impurity, it is only pushed aside,
for this it was pushed aside,
phrases.notes: For this means the corpse-impurity, and for that means the זיבה.

phrases.english: for that it was not pushed aside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects even the corrected version agreed on in steps 14 and 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the מצורע and a community of טמאי מתים who became זבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע's permission is a full היתר, which covers added impurities. Community impurity is only דחויה, which is limited to the specific impurity that was pushed aside.

steps.title: רבא flips the logic: a permission is narrow, an override is broad
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the distinction from step 16. He argues the opposite is more logical. The מצורע's היתר covers only his צרעת and not a second impurity. Community impurity is דחויה, and once impurity is pushed aside, one impurity or two makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: On the contrary, the opposite makes more sense! A מצורע was given a specific permission. It covers this impurity, but it does not cover that other impurity. But impurity in a community is simply pushed aside. So what difference does it make to me whether one impurity is pushed aside or two?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against the previous step's argument. He says the opposite reasoning is actually the more logical one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said a full היתר is stronger, so it can stretch to cover a second impurity, while a mere דחייה cannot. רבא says a היתר is a precise grant, so it covers only what the תורה allowed (the מצורע's own צרעת) and nothing extra. A דחייה means the rule of impurity has simply been set aside, so adding a second impurity changes nothing. That would support רב יוסף's ruling that the community may bring the פסח even with זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A true permission: the prohibition does not apply at all in this case
Pushed aside: the prohibition still exists but is overridden
A person with צרעת, a skin affliction that makes him טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Two opposite ways to view the same pair of concepts. Step 16 says a היתר is strong and reaches further, while a דחייה is weak and stays limited. רבא says a היתר is narrow and covers only what it was given for, while a דחייה is broad because once impurity is set aside, the number of impurities does not matter.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'permitted' (היתר) is always the stronger idea. רבא's point is that a היתר is precise and limited, while a דחייה can be all-or-nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This היתר-versus-דחייה framework shows up across ש״ס. Seeing that each side can be argued as the broader one helps you follow many later סוגיות.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
On the contrary, the opposite is more reasonable!
A leper – it is a specific permission,
phrases.notes: The תורה specifically lets a מצורע put his thumb and big toe into the courtyard to finish his purification, even though he is טמא.

phrases.english: for this impurity it was permitted
but for that impurity it was not permitted;
phrases.notes: 'That' is a second impurity he picked up, such as from a seminal emission. The permission never covered it.

phrases.english: but impurity in the community – it is overridden,
what difference is it to me if one impurity is overridden,
or if two impurities are overridden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the reasoning of step 16 by reversing which concept (היתר or דחייה) is the broader one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects step 16's claim that a full היתר extends to a second impurity while a דחייה does not.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 16 treated a היתר as stronger and wider. In fact a היתר is a precise grant limited to its specific impurity, while a דחייה sets impurity aside entirely, so one impurity or two is the same.
